home-player-center: SAS built in: tickets in and out, free play and bonus credits, with no PC needed.
Player tracking: tap a GMOOCA card on the lit ring, or use the machine's existing magstripe card reader.
Bonus wheel: players earn session points and spin for free play; the award lands on the credit meter.
Connections: Wi-Fi 6 and optional wired Ethernet to the GMOOCA app; it works standalone without them.
enterprise-floor-module: A dedicated SAS processor keeps meters, door events and tickets running even while the display system updates.
Linux display system on an industry-standard plug-in module, so there's no single-vendor lock-in.
One PoE+ network cable carries both data and power; cabinet power is the alternative.
tito-magic: Plugs into the SAS port; no PC or network.
Two taps of the service button add $100 of free play; four taps add $500. Amounts are set on a small switch.
sas-gateway: Wired, powered over the network cable, and links one machine to the GMOOCA app.
sas-gateway-wireless: A wireless version of the gateway for game rooms where running cable isn't practical.

next: Bench testing of the player tracking building blocks on development kits: the 6.2-inch screen, card taps, and SAS bonus credits on a real machine.
Display samples from shortlisted 6.2-inch panel makers. The insert is designed around the standard 6.2-inch size used by existing player tracking displays.
Circuit board layout of the Home Player Center, then a first prototype run.
Custom inserts: one universal core plus an adapter plate for each cabinet family, starting with the cabinets we own.
Software: player tracking, mini-games and rewards come with Gaming Manager 3. Gaming Manager 2 continues to be finished and tested.
TITO Magic and the smaller Gateway revision resume after the player tracking prototypes.
